purpose.summary: Recover the same identity-bound bounded-regtest upstream index after actual process death using a persistent OS-locked lease, without wiping or changing node authority.
scope: The integration parent is a signed local review checkpoint; this record does not assume it is already public main.
Only the separately opted-in daemon profile uses the new OS lease. Keep the old fixture lease semantics unchanged.
Preserve lock-file inode and identity across positive stop, real SIGKILL and upstream RocksDB reopen/resync.
Refuse unknown/partial/aliased leases and failed roots; preserve the database and keep native mining independent.
Add exact native lease rejection cases and a real-daemon crash/reopen/mining witness; retain inherited component controls and explicit limits.
exclusions: No consensus, native mempool policy, activation, default-ON option, dependency or upstream index algorithm change.
No power-loss/corruption repair claim, arbitrary history, automatic database wipe, lease unlink, identity rewrite, plugin enablement or external listener.
No incoming evidence, private history, operator data, server access, deployment, cutover, release or desktop integration.

commands: Build the independent compiled-out profile with all upstream/plugin/observer flags OFF; execute the existing native zero-subsidy mining and positive-stop smoke.
expected_results: Native mining and shutdown work without linking Rust/Chronik; no Chronik state or external peer connection is created.

commands: Build separate archival and plugin profiles with BUILD_CHRONIK_UPSTREAM_REGTEST=OFF; run unchanged exact native selections and dormant daemon controls. Keep the enabled daemon build independent.
expected_results: No Python plugin implementation is selected; setup refuses before plugin files or state are created. Linking upstream alone starts no daemon index or listener.

commands: Build the inherited default-OFF bounded regtest profile with plugins/Qt OFF. Run regtest_service.py --repetitions 3, exact native lease cases 9/6 and shutdown case 9, plus the retained native selections.
expected_results: SIGKILL releases the OS lease without unlink; the same bound root reopens through upstream setup/resync with matching transaction bytes and renewed native/indexed progress. Unknown leases and failed roots remain refused.

scenarios.command: Run the inherited real-daemon lifecycle extended with actual SIGKILL, same-root/inode reopen, raw byte parity and renewed native/indexed mining. Execute exact native lease and shutdown cases in fresh processes. Other inherited observer scenarios remain separate coverage, not this daemon's readiness.
expected_results: Three repetitions: 18 fresh daemon processes including controls, 3 shutdown processes and 6 lease-case processes. Exactly four positive stops and one SIGKILL per cycle.

Identity and lock inode unchanged, no failure marker from a healthy crash, native/indexed tips and raw transaction bytes agree, final native height 104. All disposable process groups and roots removed before exclusive path-free report creation.
The bounded 104-block witness is not a complete 288-block startup stress, power-loss or production durability proof.
failure_conditions: Wrong exact case/assertion selection, stale or changed source/view, mismatched plugin accepted, identity rewritten, disabled guard bypass, failed root adopted, native authority effect, skip, timeout, nonzero exit, instability or incomplete cleanup.

scenarios.command: Existing observer profile only, retained by chronik-port-core.yml: Run feature_chronik_token_http.py: extend to height 290 in bounded batches, disconnect below the retained projection anchor, reconsider, verify mismatched restart leaves HTTP disabled, then explicitly full-reindex. Separately exercise upstream retained-anchor and source-generation contradictions; the fixture observer closes while native progress continues.
expected_results: Inherited observer coverage only; this scenario does not establish the upstream daemon's readiness.
Both known and unknown token/transaction IDs return protobuf 503 after observer closure, never stale 200 or misleading 404.

Node RPC and chain selection continue; reconsider does not reopen observation. A persistent-tip mismatch disables HTTP on restart and logs recovery=reindex. Explicit full reindex restores canonical token metadata and byte-identical confirmed transaction output.
failure_conditions: Any accepted response after irreversible closure, missing-ID 404 from a degraded view, HTTP serving from a mismatched restarted runtime, missing mismatch diagnostic, failed canonical reindex recovery, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

limitations: Startup remains synchronous before peers in this slice; stalled storage can delay initialization or joined stop. No hard I/O latency guarantee.
SIGKILL after a confirmed healthy index is process death, not a physical power loss, torn filesystem write, arbitrary DB corruption or migration test.
Unknown or partial lease bytes, legacy fixture leases, failed markers and mismatched identities require external review; no automatic adoption or repair.
Experimental unpruned regtest only: height <= 2000, native index/pool <= 4096, 288-block capture window, 128 callback tickets and 64 MiB serialized payload. Not RSS or full-chain scaling bounds.
Plugins and public exposure remain disabled. No deployment, activation, server/desktop integration or proof promotion.
Rust registry closure remains locked; system/SDK/runner inputs remain unlocked and existing dependency security alerts remain open.
counterevidence: A supplementary single-repetition final-source retained run also refused runtime-stop-and-reopen-controls with class process-timeout at the unchanged 60-second limit. It emitted no passing report. The final-source three-cycle daemon crash/reopen witness passed, but neither that witness nor later isolated passes replace the failing retained matrix; this checkpoint is not PR-ready. A bounded local stack-sampling attempt itself exceeded its five-second diagnostic limit and yielded no usable stack; all sampler/native processes and disposable roots were cleaned.

The first complete retained matrix for this slice refused the stop/reopen group and emitted no passing report. An unchanged isolated rerun passed once in 36.26 seconds, then timed out at 60 seconds after identity_paths_and_unbound_database_fail_closed started. A separate diagnostic with detailed Boost output passed that leaf in 1.89 seconds and the complete 13-case/307-assertion group in 24.61 seconds; that detailed output deliberately fails the normal binding-path contract and is not a passing matrix report. The underlying cause remains unestablished. No timeout, assertion, selected case or cleanup requirement was relaxed.

Self-review found that the new standard-library file lock requires Rust 1.89 while the host crate still inherited workspace minimum 1.85. The crate now explicitly declares 1.89.0; CI remains pinned to 1.93.1. No dependency edge, registry tuple, checksum or Cargo lock is changed. Earlier local observations are not final-source evidence after this declaration and bounded lease-read correction.

Initial native compilation of this slice refused because the new synthetic test used a nonexistent fsbridge::ofstream alias. Use std::ofstream with explicit <fstream>; no runtime oracle, source policy or deadline was weakened.

The previous create_new-only fixture lease survives SIGKILL and cannot distinguish a dead owner safely. This slice adds an OS lease only for the daemon profile; it does not delete or guess ownership of old/unknown lock files.
Change 0049's unexplained stop/reopen matrix refusal and all preceding counterevidence remain preserved in their immutable records. Later passes do not establish their causes.

Zero-subsidy transactions and synthetic prioritisetransaction selection fees prove mechanics only. Actual inputs/outputs/fees remain zero; no economic funding or ALP lifecycle claim is made by this slice.
